questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that my destination was English speaking, and had a broad variety of courses within my field of interest.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Before leaving for Australia there was a zoom meeting with the study abroad/exchange programme at UWA where a lot of information was explained and you could ask questions. These people were also very good at responding to emails throughout the process. Upon arrival, there was an info meeting in orientation week with a further introduction to Australia, Perth, UWA and the people who we could contact in case of problems with anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: See above

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
On campus, there are 5 residential colleges a 5 min walk from uni and 15 min bike/bus ride from Perth city. They vary a bit in pricing, accommodation type and what is included. I chose Trinity residential college where I had a private room, all meals included gym, kitchens, laundry facilities and several sports opportunities and trips. 
There is also student accommodation in Perth city.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
There are resident kitchens in all wings with a big fridge and microwave and a bigger kitchen with all cooking equipment ect. 
At Trinity, breakfast, morning tea, lunch, dinner is included every day at meal time (plus fruit tea and coffee at all times)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Residential colleges are a bit more expensive than off-campus living, but with everything included it adds up to a similar cost of living. For a single semester, I found it very convenient to stay at a college where your housing is sorted before arrival and you meet a lot of friends there both Australians and other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
First you apply for the units you are interested in - apply for more than 4 just in case some are not approved. After arriving in Australia I got access to an online timetable application. In the application you add the 4 units you would like and then the app shows you what your timetable would look like. You can add/remove/change units to figure out what timetable works best for you. 
After you are done you apply for that timetable. In some units there is flexibility to choose alternative days for labs/tutorials or an online options for lectures in case you have some timetable clashes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student central and the different faculties on campus were very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was approved for 7 units and then I choose the 4 that fit best together in my timetable.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are in doubt, just message them, they are very kind and quick to respond.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two third-year units and one second-year unit that were of similar difficulty to UCPH, and I had one first-year unit (Active leadership) which was very chill and fun.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures and labs were very similar, but one thing that was quite different was the continual assessments - every lab and assignment counts 2-15% of your final grade. There are also mid-semester test which count 20-30% of the grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GENE3340 - Molecular Genetics II
MICR2209 - Intro to Infect Diseases & Immunology
NEUR3301 - Advanced Neuroscience 1
SSEH1104 - Active Leadership 1: Dev. Leader. Skills

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed all of my courses, especially GENE3340. Mark and Belinda who run the unit are super nice and helpful and every other week they held an extra lecture for those interested where they discussed articles within the field of molecular genetics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Eating out and drinks are very expensive in Australia, but in a residental college all meals are included.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks are very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Trinity residential college offer activities every week - including themed dinners, gallas, fund-raiser, inter-college sports, and trips to local attractions. Especially during orientation week, there were several activities every day. 
At uni there were also heaps of free opportunities for exchange students like free gym memberships (for 1 month), new sports opportunities (beginners squash, tennis, swimming, and others) 6 weeks for free), trips to the zoo and aquarium for all exchange students during orientation week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Buy a second-hand car (2000-3000$) or befriend someone with a car and do heaps of weekend trips! there are so many beautiful places around Perth but the public transport is not great. I bought a car with two friends and sold it again after the semester we sold for 300$ that what we bought it for. 

Kalbarri, Karijini, Exmouth, Margret River, Esperance, Denmark, Albany, and the Pinnacles - just some of the beautiful places within reach of Perth!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The people were super nice an friendly, which made it very easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to as many events and free trips during orientation week as possible. You will meet many people which makes the exchange experience a lot better.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It takes a week or two to adjust to speaking English 24/7 and the jetlag does not help;) but after that you quickly adjust.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The beautiful nature of Australia and the great effort the Australians make to honour the aboriginal land and culture. For example - every lecture at UWA starts with an acknowledgement of country (just a 30 second thing)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) The semester is shorter (only 12 weeks) and therefore more intense than at UCPH
2) The campus is quite big, so I would recommend getting a bike (there are free bikes at Trinity)
3) All exams and tests are on paper, even essays

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of help to get at UWA, so don't be afraid to ask. As a student, you can get a lot of help for free like a uni mentor, a chat with a counsellor, a therapy dog visit every Wednesday, and a great study environment. There are several libraries and big grass areas and cafes to study on campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Completing a full semester in a second language, while still having a great time and exploring the beautiful state of WA on the weekends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a good balance between during well in my units and also enjoying my time and exploring Western Australia. It takes a while to settle into a new routine, but once I figured out what worked for me I could really enjoy the experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
